turns.answer: In Video A (v1), the chef mixes butter and milk with the eggs before cooking: butter and milk are whisked together, eggs are cracked into that mixture and whisked, and the combined egg mixture is then poured into a heated pan. In Video B (v2), the eggs are shown as a separate ingredient and are whisked/poured into a pan that already contains butter; a shredded ingredient, likely cheese based on the displayed ingredients, is added and mixed during cooking. The difference is that v1 combines butter and milk directly into the eggs before cooking, while v2 appears to keep butter in the pan and add the shredded ingredient during cooking rather than before. The v2 evidence does not fully settle whether any ingredient was already mixed into the poured egg mixture, so the confirmed pre-cooking egg mixture is clear only for v1.
